I could not refute "wrong". It is a mild case: both names point to the same chamber.

What I checked:
- GET /v1/organizations/22289866: identifier TELEFON06131162234, 22 mentions. The served name is the head, with the line break.
- The buyer, winner and bidder lists for this org are all empty. It appears only as a Lot-ReviewOrg in other buyers' notices, so I read the two dated procedures and their source notices.

The two prints:
- Head, tender 990997 (TED 00783545-2023, 2023-12-22, buyer VRT Verkehrsverbund Region Trier, published on subreport). The source field BT-500 reads 'Vergabekammer Rheinland-Pfalz\nbei dem Ministerium für Wirtschaft, Verkehr, Landwirtschaft und Weinbau'. The same record gives the chamber's real contact data: phone 06131 16-2234, Stiftsstraße 9, 55116 Mainz, vergabekammer.rlp@mwvlw.rlp.de, and the MWVLW web page for the Vergabekammer. The line break is in the source itself. Apart from that, this is the chamber's full proper name.
- Majority, tender 72821 (TED 00200726-2025, 2025-03-28, buyer Studierendenwerk Vorderpfalz). BT-500 reads 'Vergabekammer Ministerium für Wirtschaft, Verkehr, Landwirtschaft und Weinbau', and BT-16 (the part name) reads 'Vergabekammer'. So the elected form is the buyer's own print: the part name put in front of the host ministry's name. It drops the chamber's actual name, 'Vergabekammer Rheinland-Pfalz', and the 'beim' link, which leaves an ungrammatical shortened form.

Why I keep "wrong":
- The new name is the same entity, but it is a shortened form of the proper name and loses the state name the chamber is known and cited by ('VK Rheinland-Pfalz'). It stays identifiable only through the ministry name, which is specific to Rheinland-Pfalz. Most readers would not know which state is meant.
- Is the head junk? Not in substance. Its only defect is a newline, which collapsing whitespace would fix. Swapping in a shortened name is not the right fix for that.
- Without the release, the v10 head_current hold would have kept this name. The head's newest print (2023-12-22) is about 1,029 days before 2026-10-16, inside the 1,095-day window. So the weak 'unfit' release (a newline) is the only reason the name changes.
- A clean full spelling was available: 'Vergabekammer Rheinland-Pfalz beim Ministerium für Wirtschaft, Verkehr, Landwirtschaft und Weinbau' (2 prints). That would have been the right name to serve.

What I could not check: where the 18 majority prints come from. The API has no review-body filter, and I did not use /v1/sql. This does not change the verdict, which rests on the quality of the name itself.
